protocol_scope: ISO 11898-1 Classical CAN (CAN CC), not CAN FD. Illustrations are not clock-accurate waveforms.

claims.claim: CAN basic physical/data-link layer roles and arbitration/ACK responsibilities
claims.locator: CAN CC data frame formats / error detection
claims.notes: LLC/MAC is conceptual; application mapping belongs in higher layer

claims.claim: Classic base frame uses 11-bit identifier; 12-bit arbitration field, 6-bit control, 0..8 bytes, CRC-15 and delimiter, ACK slot/delimiter and EOF
claims.notes: Frame field bit grouping is explained explicitly in article

claims.claim: Classic extended frame uses 11-bit base plus 18-bit extension, with SRR/IDE arbitration differences
ACK slot is acknowledged by any correctly receiving controller but not necessarily an intended application
claims.notes: ACK is not end-to-end application delivery

claims.claim: Classic CAN remote frame has RTR recessive, no data field, DLC represents expected response length; CAN FD does not support remote frames
Classic CAN transmitter inserts complementary bit after five identical bits from SOF through CRC sequence
claims.notes: Standalone example is illustrative and excludes framing, not a full controller simulation

claims.claim: Classic CAN uses CRC-15 check sequence; CAN FD changes CRC protection
claims.locator: Cyclic redundancy check in CAN CC frames
claims.notes: No CRC computation is claimed by sample code

claims.claim: Active error flag six dominant bits; passive flag six recessive bits, error delimiter eight recessive bits
claims.notes: May be extended on bus by superposed error flags

claims.claim: Classical CAN overload flag six dominant bits followed by eight recessive delimiter bits; rarely used by modern controllers
claims.notes: Do not equate arbitrary software queue overflow with an overload frame

claims.claim: Error-passive when TEC or REC exceeds 127; bus-off when TEC exceeds 255
claims.notes: Threshold summary only; individual counter update rules are more complex

claims.claim: 11-bit classical data frame 8-byte payload contains 108 unstuffed frame bits, or 111 with minimum intermission
claims.notes: Excludes bit stuffing, idle, retransmission and any error-passive suspend

claims.claim: 29-bit classical data frame 8-byte payload contains 128 unstuffed frame bits
claims.notes: Add 3 for minimum intermission; excludes stuffing

claims.claim: 11-bit classic remote frame DLC=8 contains 44 unstuffed bits, no data field
claims.notes: DLC 8 means requested length not actual payload

claims.claim: Standalone frame order, arbitration prefix, and bit stuffing diagrams
claims.notes: Original instructional drawings; rectangles are not bit-time proportional
